        "contents": "-- Users can update their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id )\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- Users can insert their own user record (during signup via trigger)\ncreate policy \"Users can insert their own user record\" on public.users\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - PROFILES TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can view their own profile\ncreate policy \"Users can view their own profile\" on public.profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  user_id in (\n    select id\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n  )\n);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - REALTIME MESSAGES TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can receive broadcasts for their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can receive broadcasts for their own user record\" on realtime.messages\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  topic like 'users:%'\n  and exists (\n    select 1\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n    and topic = 'users:' || id::text\n  )\n);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- GRANTS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Grant execute permissions for Supabase Auth hook function\n-- Trigger functions (handle_new_auth_user, validate_czu_email_domain_trigger) are invoked by triggers, not directly, so no EXECUTE grants needed\ngrant execute on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) to supabase_auth_admin;\ngrant usage on schema public to supabase_auth_admin;\nrevoke execute on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) from anon, authenticated, public;",

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can add an index like:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate index userid\non test_table\nusing btree (user_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Call functions with &#96;select&#96;\n\nYou can use &#96;select&#96; statement to improve policies that use functions. For example, instead of this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth.uid() = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can do:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis method works well for JWT functions like &#96;auth.uid()&#96; and &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; as well as &#96;security definer&#96; Functions. Wrapping the function causes an &#96;initPlan&#96; to be run by the Postgres optimizer, which allows it to \"cache\" the results per-statement, rather than calling the function on each row.\n\nCaution: You can only use this technique if the results of the query or function do not change based on the row data.\n\n### Minimize joins\n\nYou can often rewrite your Policies to avoid joins between the source and the target table. Instead, try to organize your policy to fetch all the relevant data from the target table into an array or set, then you can use an &#96;IN&#96; or &#96;ANY&#96; operation in your filter.\n\nFor example, this is an example of a slow policy which joins the source &#96;test_table&#96; to the target &#96;team_user&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  (select auth.uid()) in (\n    select user_id\n    from team_user\n    where team_user.team_id = team_id -- joins to the source \"test_table.team_id\"\n  )\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWe can rewrite this to avoid this join, and instead select the filter criteria into a set:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  team_id in (\n    select team_id\n    from team_user",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 164
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 165
          },
          {
            "text": "using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );",
            "lineNumber": 166
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 167
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 168
          },
          {
            "text": "You can add an index like:",
            "lineNumber": 169
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 170
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 171
          },
          {
            "text": "create index userid",
            "lineNumber": 172
          },
          {
            "text": "on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 173
          },
          {
            "text": "using btree (user_id);",
            "lineNumber": 174
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 175
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 176
          },
          {
            "text": "### Call functions with &#96;select&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 177
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 178
          },
          {
            "text": "You can use &#96;select&#96; statement to improve policies that use functions. For example, instead of this:",
            "lineNumber": 179
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 180
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 181
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 182
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 183
          },
          {
            "text": "using ( auth.uid() = user_id );",
            "lineNumber": 184
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 185
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 186
          },
          {
            "text": "You can do:",
            "lineNumber": 187
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 188
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 189
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 190
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": "using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "text": "This method works well for JWT functions like &#96;auth.uid()&#96; and &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; as well as &#96;security definer&#96; Functions. Wrapping the function causes an &#96;initPlan&#96; to be run by the Postgres optimizer, which allows it to \"cache\" the results per-statement, rather than calling the function on each row.",
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": "Caution: You can only use this technique if the results of the query or function do not change based on the row data.",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": "### Minimize joins",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": "You can often rewrite your Policies to avoid joins between the source and the target table. Instead, try to organize your policy to fetch all the relevant data from the target table into an array or set, then you can use an &#96;IN&#96; or &#96;ANY&#96; operation in your filter.",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "text": "For example, this is an example of a slow policy which joins the source &#96;test_table&#96; to the target &#96;team_user&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": "using (",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "text": "  (select auth.uid()) in (",
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": "    select user_id",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "text": "    from team_user",
            "lineNumber": 211
          },
          {
            "text": "    where team_user.team_id = team_id -- joins to the source \"test_table.team_id\"",
            "lineNumber": 212
          },
          {
            "text": "  )",
            "lineNumber": 213
          },
          {
            "text": ");",
            "lineNumber": 214
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 215
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 216
          },
          {
            "text": "We can rewrite this to avoid this join, and instead select the filter criteria into a set:",
            "lineNumber": 217
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "text": "using (",
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "  team_id in (",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "text": "    select team_id",
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "    from team_user",
            "lineNumber": 225
          }
        ]

reported_by IN (\n            SELECT id FROM profiles \n            WHERE user_id IN (\n                SELECT id FROM public.users \n                WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()\n            )\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Coaches and admins can resolve issues\nCREATE POLICY \"Coaches can resolve issues\" ON room_issues\n    FOR UPDATE TO authenticated\n    USING (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid() AND role IN ('coach', 'admin')));\n\n-- ----------------------------------------\n-- SCHEDULE BREAKS POLICIES\n-- ----------------------------------------\n\n-- All authenticated         "contents": "CREATE INDEX idx_profiles_is_verified ON profiles(is_verified);\nCREATE INDEX idx_pre_registered_emails_email ON pre_registered_emails(email);\nCREATE INDEX idx_pre_registered_emails_claimed_by ON pre_registered_emails(claimed_by);\nCREATE INDEX idx_verification_codes_user_id ON verification_codes(user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_verification_codes_school_email ON verification_codes(school_email);\nCREATE INDEX idx_verification_codes_expires_at ON verification_codes(expires_at);\n\n-- Function to handle new user signup\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nBEGIN\n    INSERT INTO public.profiles (id, full_name, role, team_id, is_verified, locale, created_at, updated_at)\n    VALUES (\n        NEW.id,\n        COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'full_name', ''),\n        COALESCE((NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'role')::user_role, 'student'),\n        CASE \n            WHEN NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'team_id' IS NOT NULL \n            THEN (NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'team_id')::UUID \n            ELSE NULL \n        END,\n        FALSE,\n        COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'locale', 'cs'),\n        NOW(),\n        NOW()\n    );\n    RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;\n\n-- Trigger to create profile on user signup\nCREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created\n    AFTER INSERT ON auth.users\n    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user();\n\n-- Function to update updated_at timestamp\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.update_updated_at_column()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nBEGIN\n    NEW.updated_at = NOW();\n    RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;\n\n-- Trigger to auto-update updated_at on profiles\nCREATE TRIGGER update_profiles_updated_at\n    BEFORE UPDATE ON profiles\n    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_updated_at_column();\n\n-- Row Level Security (RLS) Policies\n\n-- Enable RLS on all tables\nALTER TABLE teams ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE profiles ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE pre_registered_emails ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE verification_codes ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;",

        "contents": "/**\n * Coach dashboard for managing Training Sessions and schedule breaks\n * Only accessible by coaches and admins\n */\nexport default async function ReservationSettingsPage() {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n\n  // Check if user is coach or admin\n  const profile = await getCurrentUserProfile(supabase)\n\n  if (profile?.role !== \"coach\" &amp;&amp; profile?.role !== \"admin\") {\n    redirect(\"/dashboard/reservations\");\n  }\n\n  const isAdmin = profile?.role === \"admin\";\n\n  // Fetch all data\n  const [roomsResult, schedulesResult, breaksResult, teamsResult, issuesResult] = await Promise.all([\n    // Rooms that can have TS\n    supabase\n      .from(\"rooms\")\n      .select(\"*\")\n      .eq(\"can_have_ts\", true)\n      .order(\"code\"),\n\n    // Recurring schedules with team info\n    supabase\n      .from(\"recurring_schedules\")\n      .select(&#96;\n        *,\n        room:rooms(id, code, name),\n        team:teams(id, name)\n      &#96;)\n      .gte(\"valid_until\", new Date().toISOString().split(\"T\")[0])\n      .order(\"day_of_week\"),\n\n    // Schedule breaks\n    supabase\n      .from(\"schedule_breaks\")\n      .select(\"*\")\n      .gte(\"end_date\", new Date().toISOString().split(\"T\")[0])\n      .order(\"start_date\"),\n\n    // Teams for TS assignment\n    supabase\n      .from(\"teams\")\n      .select(\"id, name, year\")\n      .eq(\"is_active\", true)\n      .order(\"year\")\n      .order(\"name\"),\n\n    // Room issues\n    supabase\n      .from(\"room_issues\")\n      .select(&#96;\n        *,\n        room:rooms(id, code, name),\n        reporter:profiles!reported_by(id, full_name),\n        resolver:profiles!resolved_by(id, full_name)\n      &#96;)\n      .order(\"created_at\", { ascending: false })\n      .limit(50),\n  ]);\n\n  const rooms = (roomsResult.data || []) as Room[];\n  const schedules = (schedulesResult.data || []) as (RecurringSchedule &amp;         "contents": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)\n\nThese are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles). You can use these roles within your Policies using the &#96;TO&#96; clause:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles are viewable by everyone\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated, anon\nusing ( true );\n\n-- OR\n\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that &#96;for ...&#96; must be added after the table but before the roles. &#96;to ...&#96; must be added after &#96;for ...&#96;:\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nto authenticated\nfor select\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Multiple operations\n\nPostgreSQL policies do not support specifying multiple operations in a single FOR clause. You need to create separate policies for each operation.\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created and deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert, delete -- cannot create a policy on multiple operators\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true )\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true );\n\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor delete\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Helper functions\n\nSupabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.\n\n### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;\n\nReturns the ID of the user making the request.\n\n### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",

          },
          {
            "text": "## Helper functions",
            "lineNumber": 115
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 116
          },
          {
            "text": "Supabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.",
            "lineNumber": 117
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 118
          },
          {
            "text": "### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 119
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 120
          },
          {
            "text": "Returns the ID of the user making the request.",
            "lineNumber": 121
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 122
          },
          {
            "text": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 123
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "text": "Returns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:",
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",
            "lineNumber": 127
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.33754241466522217
    },

        "contents": "- When creating RLS Policies\n  - Ensure the policies cover all relevant access scenarios (e.g. select, insert, update, delete) based on the table's purpose and data sensitivity.\n  - If the table is intended for public access the policy can simply return &#96;true&#96;.\n  - RLS Policies should be granular: one policy for &#96;select&#96;, one for &#96;insert&#96; etc) and for each supabase role (&#96;anon&#96; and &#96;authenticated&#96;). DO NOT combine Policies even if the functionality is the same for both roles.\n  - Include comments explaining the rationale and intended behavior of each security policy\n- Make sure to use public schema for all tables and functions. Do not use auth schema as we do not have permissions for it in production.\n\nThe generated SQL code should be production-ready, well-documented, and aligned with Supabase's best practices.\n\n**Do not comment on auth.tables as we do not have permissions for it in production.**",

        "contents": "---\ndescription: Guidelines for writing Postgres Row Level Security policies\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Database: Create RLS policies\n\nYou're a Supabase Postgres expert in writing row level security policies. Your purpose is to generate a policy with the constraints given by the user. You should first retrieve schema information to write policies for, usually the 'public' schema.\n\nThe output should use the following instructions:\n\n- The generated SQL must be valid SQL.\n- You can use only CREATE POLICY or ALTER POLICY queries, no other queries are allowed.\n- Always use double apostrophe in SQL strings (eg. 'Night''s watch')\n- You can add short explanations to your messages.\n- The result should be a valid markdown. The SQL code should be wrapped in &#96;&#96;&#96; (including sql language tag).\n- Always use \"auth.uid()\" instead of \"current_user\".\n- SELECT policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK\n- INSERT policies should always have WITH CHECK but not USING\n- UPDATE policies should always have WITH CHECK and most often have USING\n- DELETE policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK\n- Don't use &#96;FOR ALL&#96;. Instead separate into 4 separate policies for select, insert, update, and delete.\n- The policy name should be short but detailed text explaining the policy, enclosed in double quotes.\n- Always put explanations as separate text. Never use inline SQL comments.\n- If the user asks for something that's not related to SQL policies, explain to the user\n  that you can only help with policies.\n- Discourage &#96;RESTRICTIVE&#96; policies and encourage &#96;PERMISSIVE&#96; policies, and explain why.\n\nThe output should look like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE POLICY \"My descriptive policy.\" ON books FOR INSERT to authenticated USING ( (select auth.uid()) = author_id ) WITH ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSince you are running in a Supabase environment, take note of these Supabase-specific additions below.\n\n## Authenticated and unauthenticated roles\n\nSupabase maps every request to one of the roles:\n\n- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)",

        "contents": "export async function hasLinkedProfile(\n  supabaseClient: SupabaseClient\n): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n\n}\n\n/**\n * Gets the current authenticated user's profile, optionally with team data included\n * Uses RLS policy to ensure user can only see their own profile\n * @param supabaseClient - Supabase client to use. Must be provided to use existing client.\n * @param includeTeam - Whether to fetch team data along with the profile. Defaults to false.\n * @returns The profile data with team populated (if includeTeam is true) or null if not found\n */\nexport async function getCurrentUserProfile(\n  supabaseClient: SupabaseClient,\n  includeTeam: boolean = false,\n): Promise&lt;Profile | null&gt; {\n  const { data: { user }, error: authError } = await supabaseClient.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (authError || !user) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  // Build select query conditionally based on includeTeam parameter\n  const selectQuery = includeTeam\n    ? &#96;\n      *,\n      team:teams(*)\n    &#96;\n    : \"*\";\n\n  // Query profiles - RLS policy ensures user can only see their own profile\n  // The RLS policy checks: user_id in (select id from public.users where auth_user_id = auth.uid())\n  const { data: profile, error: queryError } = await supabaseClient\n    .from(\"profiles\")\n    .select(selectQuery)\n    .limit(1)\n    .single();\n\n  // Return null if query failed or no profile found\n  if (queryError || !profile) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  // Transform the response to match Profile interface\n  // If team was fetched, extract it; otherwise set to null\n  const team = includeTeam ? ((profile as any).team || null) : null;\n\n  return {\n    ...profile,\n    team,\n  } as Profile;\n}\n\n/**\n * Creates an error URL with the given error message\n */\nexport function createErrorUrl(request: NextRequest, errorMessage: string): URL {\n  const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n}",

        "contents": "-- Users can join open reservations\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can join cowork\" ON cowork_participants\n    FOR INSERT TO authenticated\n    WITH CHECK (\n        user_id IN (\n            SELECT id FROM profiles \n            WHERE user_id IN (\n                SELECT id FROM public.users \n                WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()\n            )\n        ) AND\n        EXISTS (\n            SELECT 1 FROM reservations \n            WHERE id = reservation_id \n            AND is_cowork_open = true \n            AND status = 'active'\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Users can leave (delete their participation)\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can leave cowork\" ON cowork_participants\n    FOR DELETE TO authenticated\n    USING (\n        user_id IN (\n            SELECT id FROM profiles \n            WHERE user_id IN (\n                SELECT id FROM public.users \n                WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()\n            )\n        )\n    );\n\n-- ----------------------------------------\n-- ROOM ISSUES POLICIES\n-- ----------------------------------------\n\n-- All authenticated users can read issues\nCREATE POLICY \"Authenticated can read room_issues\" ON room_issues\n    FOR SELECT TO authenticated\n    USING (true);\n\n-- Users can report issues\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can report issues\" ON room_issues\n    FOR INSERT TO authenticated\n    WITH CHECK (\n        reported_by IN (\n            SELECT id FROM profiles \n            WHERE user_id IN (\n                SELECT id FROM public.users \n                WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()\n            )\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Users can update their own reports (before resolved)\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can update own issues\" ON room_issues\n    FOR UPDATE TO authenticated\n    USING (\n        ",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Initial schema setup\n-- Purpose: Creates complete database schema with tables, triggers, and restrictive RLS policies\n-- Affected tables: users, profiles, teams\n-- Special considerations: All RLS policies are restrictive - admin operations require service_role or application-level checks\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- ENUM TYPES\n-- ============================================================================\n\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TABLES\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create users table (custom table, separate from auth.users)\n-- Stores Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking\n-- Linked to auth.users via auth_user_id for authentication checks\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  auth_user_id uuid unique references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  google_email text not null unique,\n  suggested_work_email text,\n  verified_work_email text,\n  verified_work_email_at timestamptz,\n  google_profile_picture text,\n  google_full_name text,\n  last_otp_sent_at timestamptz,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\ncomment on table public.users is 'Custom users table storing Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking. Separate from auth.users but linked via auth_user_id for authentication.';\n\n-- Create teams table\ncreate table public.teams (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  picture text,\n  color text,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\ncomment on table public.teams is 'Team information for organizing users into groups.';\n\n-- Create profiles table (pre-created by admin, linked to user after verification)\n-- References the new users table instead of auth.users\ncreate table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),",

        "contents": "-- References the new users table instead of auth.users\ncreate table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  picture text,\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  team_id uuid references public.teams(id) on delete set null,\n  phone_number text,\n  personal_email text,\n  date_of_birth date,\n  removed_access timestamptz,\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\ncomment on table public.profiles is 'User profile data with role and team membership. Pre-created by admin, linked to user after OTP verification.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- FUNCTIONS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger function to automatically update updated_at column\ncreate or replace function public.handle_updated_at()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  new.updated_at := now();\n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_updated_at() is 'Trigger function that automatically updates the updated_at column to the current timestamp on row updates.';\n\n-- Create trigger function to populate public.users on auth.users creation\n-- Extracts Google OAuth data from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data and auth.users.email\ncreate or replace function public.handle_new_auth_user()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_google_email text;\n  v_google_full_name text;\n  v_google_profile_picture text;\n  v_raw_meta_data jsonb;\nbegin\n  v_raw_meta_data := new.raw_user_meta_data;",

    {
      "codeBlock": {

          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 119
          }
        },
        "contents": "4. **School Email Verification** - Unverified users must:\n   - Enter their school email (@pef.czu.cz)\n   - System checks if email is in pre-registered list\n   - If valid, sends 6-digit verification code\n   - User enters code to complete verification\n5. **Access Granted** - Verified users access the dashboard\n\n## Database Schema\n\n### Tables\n\n#### &#96;profiles&#96;\nExtended user info linked to Supabase auth.users\n\n| Column | Type | Nullable | Description |\n|--------|------|----------|-------------|\n| id | UUID (PK, FK → auth.users.id) | No | Links to Supabase auth |\n| full_name | TEXT | No | User's display name |\n| role | ENUM ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin') | No | User role |\n| team_id | UUID (FK → teams.id) | Yes | Assigned team (students/team leaders only) |\n| is_verified | BOOLEAN | No | School email verified? Default: false |\n| school_email | TEXT | Yes | Verified school email |\n| locale | TEXT | No | Preferred language ('cs', 'en'). Default: 'cs' |\n| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | No | Registration time |\n| updated_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | No | Last update time |\n\n#### &#96;teams&#96;\nTeam companies (tymove firmy)\n\n| Column | Type | Nullable | Description |\n|--------|------|----------|-------------|\n| id | UUID (PK) | No | Team identifier |\n| name | TEXT | No | Team name |\n| year | INTEGER | No | Cohort year (1, 2, 3) |\n| is_active | BOOLEAN | No | Still active team? Default: true |\n| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | No | Creation time |\n\n#### &#96;pre_registered_emails&#96;\nAdmin-imported student list from Excel\n\n| Column | Type | Nullable | Description |\n|--------|------|----------|-------------|\n| id | UUID (PK) | No | Record identifier |\n| email | TEXT (unique) | No | School email from Excel |\n| team_id | UUID (FK → teams.id) | No | Assigned team |\n| role | ENUM | No | Expected role |\n| full_name | TEXT | Yes | Name from Excel (optional) |\n| claimed_by | UUID (FK → profiles.id) | Yes | User who claimed this email |\n| claimed_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | Yes | When claimed |\n| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | No | Import time |\n\n#### &#96;verification_codes&#96;",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "4. **School Email Verification** - Unverified users must:",

            "text": "   - Enter their school email (@pef.czu.cz)",

          },

        },
        "contents": "Use MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Users table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth)\n-- Note: Synced via Next.js server actions, not database triggers\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  email text not null,\n  name text,\n  picture text,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\n-- Role enum for profiles (authorization)\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- Profiles table (pre-created by admin, linked to user after verification)\n-- Focus: Authentication and authorization only\ncreate table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,  -- linked after OTP verification\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  removed_access timestamptz,  -- null = active, set = revoked\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\n-- Indexes for auth queries\ncreate index profiles_user_id_idx on public.profiles(user_id);\ncreate index profiles_work_email_idx on public.profiles(work_email);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Entity Relationships\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────┐\n│   auth.users    │       │    profiles     │\n│  (Supabase)     │       │  (Auth only)    │\n├─────────────────┤       ├─────────────────┤\n│ id (uuid)       │◄──┐   │ id (uuid)       │\n│ email (google)  │   │   │ name            │\n│ ...auth fields  │   └───│ user_id (1:1)   │",

        "contents": "ALTER TABLE verification_codes ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\n\n-- Teams: Anyone authenticated can read active teams\nCREATE POLICY \"Anyone can view active teams\" ON teams\n    FOR SELECT USING (is_active = true);\n\n-- Teams: Only admins can modify teams\nCREATE POLICY \"Admins can manage teams\" ON teams\n    FOR ALL USING (\n        EXISTS (\n            SELECT 1 FROM profiles \n            WHERE profiles.id = auth.uid() \n            AND profiles.role = 'admin'\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Profiles: Users can read their own profile\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can view own profile\" ON profiles\n    FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = id);\n\n-- Profiles: Verified users can view other profiles in their team\nCREATE POLICY \"Verified users can view team profiles\" ON profiles\n    FOR SELECT USING (\n        EXISTS (\n            SELECT 1 FROM profiles AS viewer\n            WHERE viewer.id = auth.uid()\n            AND viewer.is_verified = true\n            AND (\n                viewer.team_id = profiles.team_id\n                OR viewer.role IN ('coach', 'admin')\n            )\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Profiles: Users can update their own profile\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can update own profile\" ON profiles\n    FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = id)\n    WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = id);\n\n-- Profiles: Admins can manage all profiles\nCREATE POLICY \"Admins can manage all profiles\" ON profiles\n    FOR ALL USING (\n        EXISTS (\n            SELECT 1 FROM profiles \n            WHERE profiles.id = auth.uid() \n            AND profiles.role = 'admin'\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Pre-registered emails: Users can check if their email exists\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can check pre-registered emails\" ON pre_registered_emails\n    FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL);\n\n-- Pre-registered emails: Only admins can modify\nCREATE POLICY \"Admins can manage pre-registered emails\" ON pre_registered_emails\n    FOR ALL USING (\n        EXISTS (\n            SELECT 1 FROM profiles ",

        "contents": "CREATE INDEX idx_profiles_is_verified ON profiles(is_verified);\nCREATE INDEX idx_pre_registered_emails_email ON pre_registered_emails(email);\nCREATE INDEX idx_pre_registered_emails_claimed_by ON pre_registered_emails(claimed_by);\nCREATE INDEX idx_verification_codes_user_id ON verification_codes(user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_verification_codes_school_email ON verification_codes(school_email);\nCREATE INDEX idx_verification_codes_expires_at ON verification_codes(expires_at);\n\n-- Function to handle new user signup\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nBEGIN\n    INSERT INTO public.profiles (id, full_name, role, team_id, is_verified, locale, created_at, updated_at)\n    VALUES (\n        NEW.id,\n        COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'full_name', ''),\n        COALESCE((NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'role')::user_role, 'student'),\n        CASE \n            WHEN NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'team_id' IS NOT NULL \n            THEN (NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'team_id')::UUID \n            ELSE NULL \n        END,\n        FALSE,\n        COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'locale', 'cs'),\n        NOW(),\n        NOW()\n    );\n    RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;\n\n-- Trigger to create profile on user signup\nCREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created\n    AFTER INSERT ON auth.users\n    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user();\n\n-- Function to update updated_at timestamp\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.update_updated_at_column()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nBEGIN\n    NEW.updated_at = NOW();\n    RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;\n\n-- Trigger to auto-update updated_at on profiles\nCREATE TRIGGER update_profiles_updated_at\n    BEFORE UPDATE ON profiles\n    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_updated_at_column();\n\n-- Row Level Security (RLS) Policies\n\n-- Enable RLS on all tables\nALTER TABLE teams ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE profiles ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE pre_registered_emails ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE verification_codes ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;",

        "contents": "comment on function public.link_user_to_profile() is 'Trigger function that automatically links profile rows to user rows when auth.users.email matches profiles.work_email. Matches based on currently logged in user email (auth.users.email), uid in user table row (public.users.auth_user_id), and work_email in profile table row (public.profiles.work_email).';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TRIGGERS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table to link profiles when email changes\n-- Runs AFTER UPDATE to ensure email change is committed\ndrop trigger if exists link_user_to_profile_trigger on auth.users;\n\ncreate trigger link_user_to_profile_trigger\nafter update of email on auth.users\nfor each row\nwhen (old.email is distinct from new.email)\nexecute function public.link_user_to_profile();\n\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- INITIAL DATA LINKING\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Link existing profiles to users based on current email matches\n-- This handles any existing data that needs to be linked\n-- Normalize both sides of comparison to handle case/whitespace differences\nupdate public.profiles p\nset user_id = u.id\nfrom public.users u\ninner join auth.users au on u.auth_user_id = au.id\nwhere lower(trim(p.work_email)) = lower(trim(au.email))\n  and (p.user_id is null or p.user_id = u.id);\n\ncomment on table public.profiles is 'User profile data with role and team membership. Pre-created by admin, linked to user after OTP verification. Automatically linked when auth.users.email matches profiles.work_email.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- GRANTS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Grant execute permissions for the trigger function\ngrant execute on function public.link_user_to_profile() to authenticated;",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Link users to profiles based on email matching\n-- Purpose: Automatically links profile rows to user rows when auth.users.email matches profiles.work_email\n-- Affected tables: profiles, users, auth.users\n-- Special considerations: Runs automatically when user email changes in auth.users table\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- FUNCTIONS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger function to link profiles to users based on email matching\n-- Matches auth.users.email with profiles.work_email and links via public.users\n-- Runs with SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table\ncreate or replace function public.link_user_to_profile()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_user_id uuid;\n  v_auth_email text;\nbegin\n  -- Get the email from auth.users (use NEW.email after update)\n  v_auth_email := new.email;\n  \n  -- Only proceed if email is not null and has changed\n  if v_auth_email is null or v_auth_email = '' then\n    return new;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Find the public.users row that matches this auth.users.id\n  select id into v_user_id\n  from public.users\n  where auth_user_id = new.id;\n  \n  -- If no matching public.users row found, return early\n  if v_user_id is null then\n    return new;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Link profile to user if work_email matches auth.users.email\n  -- Only update if profile exists and is not already linked to a different user\n  -- Normalize both sides of comparison to handle case/whitespace differences\n  update public.profiles\n  set user_id = v_user_id\n  where lower(trim(work_email)) = lower(trim(v_auth_email))\n    and (user_id is null or user_id = v_user_id);\n  \n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function         "contents": "export async function hasLinkedProfile(\n  supabaseClient: SupabaseClient\n): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n\n}\n\n/**\n * Gets the current authenticated user's profile, optionally with team data included\n * Uses RLS policy to ensure user can only see their own profile\n * @param supabaseClient - Supabase client to use. Must be provided to use existing client.\n * @param includeTeam - Whether to fetch team data along with the profile. Defaults to false.\n * @returns The profile data with team populated (if includeTeam is true) or null if not found\n */\nexport async function getCurrentUserProfile(\n  supabaseClient: SupabaseClient,\n  includeTeam: boolean = false,\n): Promise&lt;Profile | null&gt; {\n  const { data: { user }, error: authError } = await supabaseClient.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (authError || !user) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  // Build select query conditionally based on includeTeam parameter\n  const selectQuery = includeTeam\n    ? &#96;\n      *,\n      team:teams(*)\n    &#96;\n    : \"*\";\n\n  // Query profiles - RLS policy ensures user can only see their own profile\n  // The RLS policy checks: user_id in (select id from public.users where auth_user_id = auth.uid())\n  const { data: profile, error: queryError } = await supabaseClient\n    .from(\"profiles\")\n    .select(selectQuery)\n    .limit(1)\n    .single();\n\n  // Return null if query failed or no profile found\n  if (queryError || !profile) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  // Transform the response to match Profile interface\n  // Supabase returns foreign key relationships as objects (not arrays) for many-to-one relationships\n  // If team was fetched, extract it; otherwise set to null\n  let team: Team | null = null;\n  if (includeTeam) {\n    const teamData = (profile as any).team;\n    // Handle both array and object responses (though it should be an object for many-to-one)\n    if (Array.isArray(teamData)) {\n      team = teamData.length &gt; 0 ? (teamData[0] as Team) : null;\n    } else if (teamData &amp;&amp; typeof teamData === 'object') {\n      team = teamData as Team;\n    }\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | No | Import time |\n\n#### &#96;verification_codes&#96;\nTemporary codes for school email verification\n\n| Column | Type | Nullable | Description |\n|--------|------|----------|-------------|\n| id | UUID (PK) | No | Code identifier |\n| user_id | UUID (FK → profiles.id) | No | Who requested |\n| school_email | TEXT | No | Email to verify |\n| code | TEXT | No | 6-digit code |\n| expires_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | No | Code expiration (10-15 min) |\n| attempts | INTEGER | No | Failed attempts count. Default: 0 |\n| used | BOOLEAN | No | Already used? Default: false |\n| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | No | Creation time |\n\n### Database Trigger\n\nOn new user signup (auth.users insert), automatically create a profile record:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nBEGIN\n  INSERT INTO public.profiles (id, full_name, role, is_verified, created_at, updated_at)\n  VALUES (\n    NEW.id,\n    COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'full_name', ''),\n    COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'role', 'student'),\n    FALSE,\n    NOW(),\n    NOW()\n  );\n  RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;\n\nCREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created\n  AFTER INSERT ON auth.users\n  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## UI Screens\n\n### 1. Landing Page (&#96;/&#96;)\n\nMinimal design with Tappka branding:\n- Tappka logo/name\n- Subtitle: \"Studentsky portal Tiimiakatemia\"\n- Login form (email, password)\n- \"Prihlasit se\" button (TAP Red)\n- \"Nemas ucet? Zaregistrovat se\" link\n- Language toggle (CZ/EN)\n\n### 2. Registration Page (&#96;/auth/sign-up&#96;)\n\nForm fields:\n- Full name (required)\n- Email (required) - personal email for login\n- Password (required)\n- Role dropdown (required): Student, Team Leader, Coach, Admin\n- Team dropdown (required if Student/Team Leader): List of active teams\n- \"Zaregistrovat se\" button\n- \"Uz mas ucet?         "contents": "│ email (google)  │   │   │ name            │\n│ ...auth fields  │   └───│ user_id (1:1)   │\n└─────────────────┘       │ work_email      │\n                          │ role (enum)     │\n                          │ removed_access  │\n                          │ removed_access_by│──┐\n                          │ created_at      │  │\n                          │ updated_at      │  │\n                          └─────────────────┘  │\n                                    ▲          │\n                                    └──────────┘ (self-reference)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Verification Logic\n\n- **Unverified**: &#96;profiles.user_id IS NULL&#96; → User logged in with Google but hasn't verified work email\n- **Pending Approval**: Work email verified via OTP, but no profile exists with that email\n- **Verified &amp; Active**: &#96;profiles.user_id IS NOT NULL AND profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **Access Revoked**: &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NOT NULL&#96;\n\n## Constants\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// lib/constants/auth.ts\nexport const ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS = [\n  'studenti.czu.cz',\n  'pef.czu.cz',\n] as const;\n\nexport const isValidWorkEmailDomain = (email: string): boolean =&gt; {\n  const domain = email.split('@')[1]?.toLowerCase();\n  return ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS.includes(domain as any);\n};\n\n// Profile roles (matches database enum)\nexport const PROFILE_ROLES = ['student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin'] as const;\nexport type ProfileRole = typeof PROFILE_ROLES[number];\n\n// Role hierarchy for permission checks\nexport const ROLE_HIERARCHY: Record&lt;ProfileRole, number&gt; = {\n  student: 0,\n  team_leader: 1,\n  coach: 2,\n  admin: 3,\n} as const;\n\nexport const hasMinimumRole = (userRole: ProfileRole, requiredRole: ProfileRole): boolean =&gt; {\n  return ROLE_HIERARCHY[userRole] &gt;= ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole];\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/work_email_auth_system_467a2b18.plan.md",
        "range": {

        },
        "contents": "## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles table for auth checks\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Seed test data into profiles table for auth testing\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer Only)\n\n1. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n2. **No RLS or Functions**:\n\n   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "  v_has_linked_profile boolean;\nbegin\n  if tg_op != 'UPDATE' then\n    return NEW;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Check if user has a linked profile before allowing email changes\n  -- Find the public.users row that matches this auth.users.id\n  select id into v_user_id\n  from public.users\n  where auth_user_id = new.id;\n\n  -- If user exists, check if they have a linked profile\n  if v_user_id is not null then\n    select exists (\n      select 1\n      from public.profiles\n      where user_id = v_user_id\n    ) into v_has_linked_profile;\n\n    -- If user has a linked profile, prevent email changes\n    if v_has_linked_profile then\n      if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n        raise exception 'Cannot change email address once linked to a profile. Your email is used to maintain your profile connection.';\n      end if;\n      \n      if OLD.email_change is distinct from NEW.email_change then\n        raise exception 'Cannot change email address once linked to a profile. Your email is used to maintain your profile connection.';\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Continue with existing domain validation for email_change\n  if OLD.email_change is distinct from NEW.email_change then\n    v_email_change := NEW.email_change;\n    \n    if v_email_change is not null and v_email_change != '' then\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email_change, '@', 2));\n      \n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Continue with existing domain validation for email\n  if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n    v_email := NEW.email;\n    \n    if v_email is not null and v_email != '' then\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email, '@', 2));\n      \n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  return NEW;\nend;\n$$;",

        "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}\n        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]\n        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]\n        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}\n        L --&gt; M\n        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]\n        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]\n        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}\n        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]\n        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;\n\n   - Client-side: Immediate feedback\n   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called\n\n2. **After OTP (Profile Linking)**: Check if a profile exists for the verified work email\n\n   - If profile exists with that work_email → link profile to auth.user\n   - If no profile exists → show \"Pending Approval\" (admin must create profile first)\n   - Checked on every request via middleware\n\n## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)\n\nTwo tables with **no RLS** - all access control is handled in Next.js:\n\n1. **&#96;users&#96;** - Custom table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth), synced via Next.js server actions\n2. **&#96;profiles&#96;** - User authentication profile data with role and access control\n\n**Important**: No Supabase functions, triggers, or RLS policies. All business logic lives in Next.js.\n\nUse MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.",

        "contents": "CREATE POLICY \"Admins can manage pre-registered emails\" ON pre_registered_emails\n    FOR ALL USING (\n        EXISTS (\n            SELECT 1 FROM profiles \n            WHERE profiles.id = auth.uid() \n            AND profiles.role = 'admin'\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Verification codes: Users can only see their own codes\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can view own verification codes\" ON verification_codes\n    FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);\n\n-- Verification codes: Users can create codes for themselves\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can create own verification codes\" ON verification_codes\n    FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\n\n-- Verification codes: Users can update their own codes (for attempts/used)\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can update own verification codes\" ON verification_codes\n    FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id)\n    WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\n\n-- Verification codes: Admins can manage all codes\nCREATE POLICY \"Admins can manage verification codes\" ON verification_codes\n    FOR ALL USING (\n        EXISTS (\n            SELECT 1 FROM profiles \n            WHERE profiles.id = auth.uid() \n            AND profiles.role = 'admin'\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Insert some sample teams for development\nINSERT INTO teams (name, year, is_active) VALUES\n    ('Tuuli', 1, true),\n    ('Tuuli', 1, true),\n    ('Impact', 2, true),\n    ('Growth', 2, true),\n    ('Legacy', 3, true);",

        "contents": "export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {\n\n\n    // Check if code matches\n    if (verificationCode.code !== code) {\n      // Increment attempts\n      await supabase\n        .from(\"verification_codes\")\n        .update({ attempts: verificationCode.attempts + 1 })\n        .eq(\"id\", verificationCode.id);\n\n      const remainingAttempts = MAX_ATTEMPTS - verificationCode.attempts - 1;\n      return NextResponse.json(\n        {\n          error: &#96;Neplatný kód. Zbývající pokusy: ${remainingAttempts}&#96;,\n        },\n        { status: 400 }\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Code is valid! Mark as used\n    await supabase\n      .from(\"verification_codes\")\n      .update({ used: true })\n      .eq(\"id\", verificationCode.id);\n\n    // Get role and team from pre_registered_emails\n    const { data: preRegistered, error: preRegError } = await supabase\n      .from(\"pre_registered_emails\")\n      .select(\"role, team_id\")\n      .eq(\"email\", school_email.toLowerCase())\n      .single();\n\n    if (preRegError || !preRegistered) {\n      console.error(\"Failed to get pre_registered_emails:\", preRegError);\n      return NextResponse.json(\n        { error: \"Nepodařilo se načíst data z registrace\" },\n        { status: 500 }\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Update profile: set is_verified, school_email, role, and team_id from pre_registered\n    const { error: profileError } = await supabase\n      .from(\"profiles\")\n      .update({\n        is_verified: true,\n        school_email: school_email.toLowerCase(),\n        role: preRegistered.role,\n        team_id: preRegistered.team_id,\n      })\n      .eq(\"id\", user.id);\n\n    if (profileError) {\n      console.error(\"Failed to update profile:\", profileError);\n      return NextResponse.json(\n        { error: \"Nepodařilo se aktualizovat profil\" },\n        { status: 500 }\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Claim the pre-registered email\n    await supabase\n      .from(\"pre_registered_emails\")\n      .update({\n        claimed_by: user.id,\n        claimed_at: new Date().toISOString(),\n      })\n      .eq(\"email\", school_email.toLowerCase());\n\n    return NextResponse.json({\n      success: true,\n      verified: true,\n\n}",

        "contents": "CREATE POLICY \"Users can update own reservations\" ON reservations\n    FOR UPDATE TO authenticated\n    USING (\n        user_id IN (\n            SELECT id FROM profiles \n            WHERE user_id IN (\n                SELECT id FROM public.users \n                WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()\n            )\n        )\n    )\n    WITH CHECK (\n        user_id IN (\n            SELECT id FROM profiles \n            WHERE user_id IN (\n                SELECT id FROM public.users \n                WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()\n            )\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Users can delete (cancel) their own reservations\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can delete own reservations\" ON reservations\n    FOR DELETE TO authenticated\n    USING (\n        user_id IN (\n            SELECT id FROM profiles \n            WHERE user_id IN (\n                SELECT id FROM public.users \n                WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()\n            )\n        )\n    );\n\n-- Coaches can manage TS and HC reservations\nCREATE POLICY \"Coaches can manage TS reservations\" ON reservations\n    FOR ALL TO authenticated\n    USING (\n        reservation_type IN ('training_session', 'houston_calling') AND\n        EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid() AND role IN ('coach', 'admin'))\n    )\n    WITH CHECK (\n        reservation_type IN ('training_session', 'houston_calling') AND\n        EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid() AND role IN ('coach', 'admin'))\n    );\n\n-- ----------------------------------------\n-- COWORK PARTICIPANTS POLICIES\n-- ----------------------------------------\n\n-- All authenticated users can read participants\nCREATE POLICY \"Authenticated can read cowork_participants\" ON cowork_participants\n    FOR SELECT TO authenticated\n    USING (true);\n\n-- Users can join open reservations\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can join cowork\" ON cowork_participants\n    FOR INSERT TO authenticated\n    WITH CHECK (\n        ",

        "contents": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.\n- &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; - cannot be updated by the user, so it's a good place to store authorization data.\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function is extremely versatile. For example, if you store some team data inside &#96;app_metadata&#96;, you can use it to determine whether a particular user belongs to a team. For example, if this was an array of IDs:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"User is in team\"\non my_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( team_id in (select auth.jwt() -&gt; 'app_metadata' -&gt; 'teams'));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### MFA\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function can be used to check for [Multi-Factor Authentication](mdc:docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#enforce-rules-for-mfa-logins). For example, you could restrict a user from updating their profile unless they have at least 2 levels of authentication (Assurance Level 2):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Restrict updates.\"\non profiles\nas restrictive\nfor update\nto authenticated using (\n  (select auth.jwt()-&gt;&gt;'aal') = 'aal2'\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## RLS performance recommendations\n\nEvery authorization system has an impact on performance. While row level security is powerful, the performance impact is important to keep in mind. This is especially true for queries that scan every row in a table - like many &#96;select&#96; operations, including those using limit, offset, and ordering.\n\nBased on a series of [tests](mdc:https:/github.com/GaryAustin1/RLS-Performance), we have a few recommendations for RLS:\n\n### Add indexes\n\nMake sure you've added [indexes](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/indexes) on any columns used within the Policies which are not already indexed (or primary keys). For a Policy like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",

## Summary

Fixed the issue where `profile.team` was null in `/dashboard`. Changes:

### 1. Created RLS policy migration (`20260201132717_add_teams_rls_policies.sql`)
   - The `teams` table had RLS enabled but no policies, blocking reads
   - Added a policy allowing authenticated users to read teams
   - Required for foreign key relationships like `team:teams(*)` in profile queries

### 2. Updated `getCurrentUserProfile` function
   - Improved team extraction to handle both array and object responses
   - Properly removes the `team` property from the profile object before spreading to avoid duplication
   - Added error logging for debugging

### 3. Verified dashboard usage
   - The dashboard correctly calls `getCurrentUserProfile(supabase, true)` to include team data
   - The team display logic properly handles null teams

After applying the migration, the team should be fetched and displayed correctly in the dashboard. The team will show:
- Team name (`profile.team.name`)
- Team year (`profile.team.year`) as "X. ročník"
- Or "Bez týmu" if the user has no team assigned

Run the migration to apply the RLS policy, then the team data should be functional in the dashboard.
